clues.text: In the hill country of Ephraim, a man told his mother he had taken her eleven hundred shekels of silver.
During the time of the judges, a mother gave two hundred shekels to a silversmith for an idol placed in her son's house.
When Israel had no king, this man kept a shrine, made an ephod and household idols, and made his son a priest.
He offered a wandering young Levite from Bethlehem ten shekels of silver a year, clothes, and food to be his priest.
After a Levite became his household priest, he said, "Now I know that the LORD will be good to me."
Five spies from the tribe of Dan, searching for land, spent the night at his house in Ephraim.
When the Danites took his gods and his priest, he and his neighbors overtook them, then turned home because they were too strong.
